stem: An RN is asked to perform an intervention that the nurse knows is outside the RN's legal scope of practice in the jurisdiction. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Perform the intervention once because a provider's request temporarily expands the RN's legal scope when the client needs the service.
options.B: Perform the intervention if another RN agrees to observe because peer presence converts an out-of-scope activity into authorized nursing practice.
options.C: Do not perform the out-of-scope intervention; clarify and escalate the request through appropriate channels and follow current law and facility policy.
options.D: Delegate the intervention to assistive personnel because delegation transfers the legal scope restriction from the RN to the person receiving the task.

rationale: The 2026 NCSBN Test Plan requires nurses to recognize professional limitations, utilize resources and provide care within legal scope of practice. If the intervention is known to be outside the RN's legal scope, C preserves that boundary while using appropriate organizational channels to resolve the care need. A provider request or peer observation does not expand statutory scope, and delegation does not transfer an out-of-scope activity to assistive personnel.
educational_objective: Respond appropriately when asked to perform an intervention outside the RN's legal scope by declining the act and escalating through lawful organizational channels.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Appendix A, Management of Care, Legal Rights and Responsibilities, printed p.22: recognize limitations and utilize resources; provide care within legal scope of practice.
source_claim_supported: The RN should not perform a known out-of-scope intervention and should use appropriate resources/policy to resolve the request.

source_original.stem: An RN is asked to perform an intervention that the nurse knows is outside the RN's legal scope of practice in the jurisdiction. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Perform the intervention once because a provider's request temporarily expands the RN's legal scope when the client needs the service.
options.B: Perform the intervention if another RN agrees to observe because peer presence converts an out-of-scope activity into authorized nursing practice.
options.C: Do not perform the out-of-scope intervention; clarify and escalate the request through appropriate channels and follow current law and facility policy.
options.D: Delegate the intervention to assistive personnel because delegation transfers the legal scope restriction from the RN to the person receiving the task.

source_original.rationale: NCSBN identifies practice within legal scope and recognition of professional limitations as Management of Care responsibilities. Option C is the only response that preserves legal scope while using appropriate organizational channels to resolve the client's care need. A provider request or peer observation does not expand statutory scope, and an RN cannot delegate an intervention that is outside the RN's own authorized scope to assistive personnel.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Stem explicitly states the act is legally out of scope, avoiding jurisdictional ambiguity.

distractor_audit.A: Provider request does not change legal scope
distractor_audit.B: Peer observation does not change legal scope
distractor_audit.D: Delegation cannot transfer an out-of-scope act

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C preserves legal scope and addresses the request.
